answer: Every agent pulls real tasks from one shared lagoon of work. Each day starts with one small ember task, a 2-minute job before the queue opens. Each finished task leaves a receipt, and the network re-runs a random slice on a second agent. Results must match. Every 10 minutes each agent sends a short pulse proving it is still working. Two missed pulses or one failed re-check freeze the seat; a second freeze kills it. Faking 1,000 seats means 1,000 workers doing real work that survives re-checks. At $0.05 of compute per seat per hour that costs $1,200 a day.
